reaction.reported_reaction: Photocatalytic hydrogen generation from methanol/water solution under visible light

evidence.text_snippet: The samples 3.5 wt.% Niacac-based NPs/TiO2 and 3.5 wt.% Niformate-based NPs/TiO2 were tested under visible light, showing a slight activity with hydrogen generation rates of 1.5 and 0.6 µmol gcat.−1 h−1, respectively.

The samples 3.5 wt.% Niacac-based NPs/TiO2 and 3.5 wt.% Niformate-based NPs/TiO2 were tested under visible light, showing a slight activity with hydrogen generation rates of 1.5 and 0.6 µmol gcat.−1 h−1, respectively.

The sample 0.1 wt.% Ni acac-based NPs/TiO2 shows a higher TRMC signal than bare TiO2 (Figure 5b) under visible excitation, but the hydrogen generation rate (0.4 µmol gcat.−1 h−1) was lower than that of 3.5 wt.% Ni acac-based NPs/TiO2.

For visible light experiments, a 300 W LOT-Oriel Xenon Lamp (250 to 2000 nm) equipped with a water filter (a large quartz cell) was positioned between the lamp and the reactor to block the infrared light and prevent sample heating. An optical filter was used to limit irradiation to the visible (λ≥ 420 nm).

The stability of the photocatalyst with cycling was also studied. After the photocatalytic test, the reactor was covered with aluminum foil and put in the dark. The next day, the reactor was degassed again and irradiated under the same conditions until 5 cycles were completed.
Commercial titania (TiO2-P25, 80% anatase, and 20% rutile, Evonik, Essen, Germany) was used as photocatalytic support.
